name: Ranginui
role: Sky father whose union with the earth mother begins the world
fun_fact: Rangi's weeping for Papa is often given as the origin of rain and dew.

name: Papatūānuku
role: Earth mother and source of the land
fun_fact: Her name is often shortened to Papa, and the land is spoken of as her body.

name: Tāne
role: God of forests, birds and human creation, who separated his parents
fun_fact: Tāne is credited with shaping the first woman, Hineahuone, from clay and breathing life into her.

name: Tangaroa
role: God of the sea and its creatures
fun_fact: Tangaroa's children include fish and reptiles, and the sea's abundance is described as his gift.

name: Tāwhirimātea
role: God of storms, winds and weather
fun_fact: His anger at the separation of his parents is why storms still come from the sky.

name: Māui
role: Trickster demigod who slowed the sun and fished up islands
fun_fact: Māui's fishhook was made from his grandmother's jawbone, and with it he fished up the North Island.

name: Rata
role: Canoe builder who learned that the forest must be asked
fun_fact: In some Māori versions the hākuturi build Rata a canoe after he apologises, naming it Niwaru.

name: Pele
role: Hawaiian volcano goddess and keeper of the fire
fun_fact: Pele is a living akua for many Hawaiians, and her home at Halema'uma'u is treated as sacred ground.

name: Kamapua'a
role: Hawaiian pig god and shape-shifter, rival and lover of Pele
fun_fact: Kamapua'a was born on O'ahu, and his name means 'pig child' in Hawaiian.

name: Hina
role: Moon goddess and ancestral woman of several island traditions
fun_fact: Hina's name is connected with the moon, and in some tellings she leaves the world to live there.
